context: Al-An'am is Makkan and belongs to the last stretch of the Makkan years, when the argument with Quraysh had hardened and neither side expected the other to move. Its audience acknowledged Allah as creator and still assigned Him partners, and they had built a law of their own around livestock and crops: portions set aside for their gods, animals whose backs were declared forbidden, unborn young reserved for the men and denied to the women.

That setting explains the method. Al-An'am does not preach so much as litigate, and the command Say is issued to the Prophet ﷺ dozens of times, each one handing him a sentence for a specific objection. Cattle, which give the surah its name, arrive only from verse 136, by which point the ground is prepared: if Allah alone creates, provides and knows, nobody else has standing to declare a camel unlawful.
name_story: The name comes from the an'am, the grazing livestock, taken up in the closing third where the surah lists what Quraysh had invented: crops divided between Allah and partners, cattle dedicated so that an idol's name was spoken over them, the eight pairs argued through at verses 143 and 144. Naming a surah of sustained theology after farm animals keeps attention on where the theology was meant to land.

movements.note: The surah praises the One who made the darknesses and the light, then turns to generations already destroyed and to the scene where those who denied the meeting ask to be sent back.

movements.h: It is not you they deny
movements.note: The Prophet ﷺ is told the rejection is not aimed at him, with earlier messengers as precedent. Verse 59 holds the keys of the unseen, alongside the order not to drive away the poor who call on their Lord morning and evening.
A star, then the moon, then the sun, each rejected as it sets. Ibrahim then heads a list naming eighteen prophets in four verses, and the Prophet ﷺ is told to follow their guidance.

movements.h: They did not appraise Him rightly
movements.note: The splitting of the seed, the stations of the sun and moon, and the warning at verse 108 against insulting the idols of others, since the insult comes back.
How a false religion is built, through embellished talk passed between people, and then the practices themselves: harvests divided with partners, children killed out of poverty, cattle set aside.

Against their list, a real one. Verses 151 to 153 set out what is prohibited and name this the straight path, and the surah closes by assigning prayer, sacrifice, living and dying to the Lord of the worlds.

themes.d: The case for one God is built from premises the Makkans already accepted, which is why the surah keeps asking who provides, who hears, who owns the night.
Twice, at verses 12 and 54, Allah is said to have decreed mercy upon Himself, and both statements sit inside passages about denial and ruin rather than at the end.

themes.t: The limits of what people know
themes.d: With Him are the keys of the unseen, and no leaf falls without His knowledge. Ignorance becomes the reason to stop legislating: people who cannot see a seed split have no basis for forbidding an animal.

What a person eats and forbids is treated as the visible test of what he believes about God. Jurists later differed over the details, including meat slaughtered without the name of Allah being said over it.

heart: Recited slowly, Al-An'am assumes that belief is something a person can reason toward and then live from. Its pace is deliberate and it rarely raises its voice. A reader who takes it in long sittings notices how often it answers an objection nobody has raised yet, which is a way of clearing ground ahead of a person's own doubts.

Two passages tend to stay. The first is Ibrahim under the night sky, rejecting each light as it sets, a mind reaching tawhid without a teacher. The second is verse 162, where prayer, sacrifice, life and death are handed over in one sentence. Both appear in the supplication that opens the prayer, reported from the Prophet ﷺ by 'Ali in Sahih Muslim 771a.

passages.why: The keys of the unseen, the falling leaf, the grain in the darkness of the earth. Nowhere else does the surah measure so plainly the distance between what Allah knows and what anyone else can reach.
Ibrahim's conclusion once the star, the moon and the sun have set. The wording belongs to the opening supplication of the prayer in Sahih Muslim 771a.
What is genuinely forbidden, answering a list people invented. It runs from associating partners with Allah to killing children out of poverty, and closes by naming the path.
Prayer, sacrifice, living and dying assigned in one line. Short enough to hold in memory and wide enough to summarise the surah.

connections.why: Al-A'raf follows immediately and takes the same argument into history, showing what became of the towns that decided otherwise.
An-Nahl returns to the invented prohibitions and names the fault outright, warning against tongues that assert this is lawful and this is unlawful.

virtue.text: No authentic report establishes a specific merit for reciting Al-An'am. What circulates instead concerns the manner of its revelation, that it came down complete at night escorted by seventy thousand angels, recorded by at-Tabarani and in another wording by al-Hakim; the critics differ over those chains, and in any case they say nothing about a reward for reciting. Its standing rests on its content, the longest sustained argument for tawhid revealed in Makkah.
virtue.src: no virtue-of-recitation report; the revelation report in at-Tabarani 12/215 and al-Hakim 2/314, grading disputed
